hypotheses.title: Parser rebuilds the array dimension list on every [] suffix, making array type descriptors O(d^2) to parse
hypotheses.issue: parser/parser.go:(*ballerinaParser).createArrayTypeDesc is called once per `[...]` suffix while parsing an array type descriptor (via parseArrayTypeDescriptor, getArrayTypeDesc from parseAsArrayTypeDesc/parseTypedBindingPatternTypeRhs, and parseArrayTypeDescriptorNode). When the member type is already an ARRAY_TYPE_DESC it copies every existing dimension node into a fresh, non-pre-sized slice, appends the new dimension, and builds a brand-new st.CreateNodeList(...) plus a new STArrayTypeDescriptorNode; CreateNodeList -> createNodeAndAddChildren -> addChildren/updateWidth walks all children again. A type with d dimensions therefore costs 1+2+...+d copies and width recomputations, and the d-1 intermediate lists/nodes become garbage. On the reproducer this function is ~95% of all bytes allocated by the compile and ~49% of CPU plus ~32% GC; it also shows up (46 MB alloc) on corpus/bench/10-bench/nested-expressions-v.bal which uses 32-dimension arrays. Real code rarely has many dimensions, so practical impact is mainly on deep/generated types.

reproducer.generator:
# Generates a Ballerina program with a single array type descriptor of N dimensions.
# usage: python3 gen_arraydims.py N > out.bal
import sys
n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 6000
print("import ballerina/io;\n")
print("public function main() {")
print("    int" + "[]" * n + " y = [];")
print("    io:println(y.length());")
print("}")
reproducer.command: python3 gen_arraydims.py 6000 > arraydims.bal && go build -o /tmp/bal ./cli/cmd && /tmp/bal run --stats arraydims.bal  (or: ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> arraydims.bal)

hypotheses.baseline: main cc62d6d6, N=6000: Parse ~725-800 ms of ~0.90 s total wall, maxrss ~96 MB. N=3000 parse ~185-220 ms; N=1500 ~52-70 ms (parse x4 per doubling of N). hyperfine wall: N=1500 120 ms, N=3000 289 ms, N=6000 916 ms.

hypotheses.fix_approach: Kept createArrayTypeDesc as the single node-building point (callers pass the partially built array node through mutually recursive parse functions, so restructuring them to collect dimensions would be invasive). Added an append operation on st.STNodeList that returns a new list in amortized O(1): it reuses the backing array's spare capacity when the old list exclusively owns it (ownership flag handed to the new list; otherwise copy into a 2*len+1 slice so an older list extended twice never clobbers a newer one), and computes the four width fields incrementally from the old list's widths plus the new child (matching updateWidth exactly incl. uint16 wraparound) instead of re-walking all children; diagnostics flag is OR'ed in. Falls back to the full CreateNodeList path if the list has its own diagnostics or no non-zero-width child. ChildBuckets() was capped to len (s[:n:n]) so external appends can't write into spare capacity. A temporary assertion comparing every appended list against a CreateNodeList rebuild (widths, flags, children) passed across make test and manual recovery cases. Simpler alternative for the real fix: accumulate dimensions in the parse loops and build once. Note: go test ./parser/ shows ~5078 failures on main too (missing golden JSON under parser/testdata in this checkout) — unrelated; make test passes.

notes: Other observations from exploration (not pursued): parser error recovery is extremely slow on nested syntax errors (20-deep nested `function () returns int {...}()` with errors takes ~3.9s in seekInAlternativesPaths/seekMatchInSubTree; depth 200 >100s); CompilerEnvironment.GetSymbol takes two RLocks per lookup (~1-3% CPU, too small).
